title: Weight Decay Shrinks the Fit
tagline: Add one penalty term, lambda times the squared weight norm, and watch a wild overfit calm into a smooth generalizing curve
summary: A degree-9 polynomial threads fifteen noisy points and wiggles violently between them with enormous coefficients. Ridge regression adds a lambda times ||w||^2 penalty that taxes big weights. Drag lambda on a log scale from near-zero (wild overfit) to large (flat underfit) and watch the fitted curve relax onto the true function, the coefficient bars collapse toward zero, ||w||^2 shrink monotonically, and the test error trace out its classic U-shaped sweet spot. The ridge normal equations are solved in closed form live with a tiny Gaussian-elimination solver.
highlights: Drag a log-scale lambda slider from wild overfit to flat underfit and watch a degree-9 ridge fit relax onto the true curve in real time.
See ||w||^2 shrink monotonically as lambda grows, plotted on log-log axes with a live marker at your current penalty.
Watch train and test error trace the classic bias-variance U-shape, with the test minimum marking the lambda you actually want.
A coefficient bar chart shows every weight collapsing toward zero, exposing that overfit means huge canceling coefficients, not just many terms.
The ridge normal equations (Phi^T Phi + lambda I) w = Phi^T y are solved in closed form in the browser with a tiny Gaussian-elimination routine.
